comparisons.title: GPT-5.6: our runs vs OpenAI's chart
comparisons.claim: At all three settings OpenAI charted, fast-agent scored higher and cost less per task.
comparisons.caveat: OpenAI's figures are launch-chart claims without trial data; ours are 445 trials each, submitted but not on the official leaderboard.

comparisons.title: Sol high on fast-agent vs Fable 5 on Claude Code
comparisons.claim: Same 89 tasks, five attempts each. fast-agent + Sol high scores 4.4 points higher at less than half the published cost.
comparisons.caveat: Different models and reasoning settings; this compares complete configurations, not harnesses.

comparisons.title: Six-hour value runs
comparisons.claim: Three low-cost models, 82–85% with a six-hour agent timeout, for $30–$78 a run.
comparisons.caveat: Non-standard six-hour timeout. Not comparable with standard-timeout leaderboard rows.

comparisons.title: Grok 4.6 medium vs Opus 4.8 on Claude Code
comparisons.claim: Grok 4.6 medium on fast-agent solves 39 more trials than Opus 4.8 on Claude Code, for about two-thirds of the cost.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.blurb: 89 tasks, five attempts each, with every trial published.

methodology.title: How we ran and scored Terminal-Bench 2.1.

points.title: Scoring
points.text: Every run is 89 tasks × 5 attempts. Scores count all 445 slots, so a missing or errored attempt scores zero. ± is one standard error, clustered by task.

points.title: Our runs
points.text: Submitted to the Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard, which closed community submissions before review, so they're provisional. Every trial is public on the Harbor Hub.

points.title: Comparators and claims
points.text: Leaderboard rows use the trials the official row lists and its published score and cost. Vendor claims are shown as published, with no trials behind them.

points.title: Costs
points.text: Our costs are Harbor's recorded token costs, not billed spend; ~ marks an estimate. Six-hour runs use a non-standard 21,600-second timeout and aren't comparable with standard rows.

points.title: Safety allowance
points.text: An optional scenario, off by default: trials a provider safety stop or refusal ended count as passes when a reference model passed that task at least 4 times in 5: Claude Haiku 5.5 high for Anthropic models, GPT-6 Luna high for the rest. It is a what-if, never a measured score, and is marked wherever it is on.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0 · 19-task subset
benchmarks.blurb: 19 of Terminal-Bench 4.0's 66 tasks, five attempts each. Leaderboard rows are cut to the same 19 tasks; their full 66-task runs are on each run page.

methodology.title: Why 19 tasks, and how far to trust them.

points.title: The subset
points.text: 19 of Terminal-Bench 4.0's 66 tasks, five attempts each. Every task runs in a single container without a GPU on HF Jobs, and none drew a safety refusal on the leaderboard.

points.title: Representative?
points.text: On 26 leaderboard rows, subset scores land within ±5 points of the full score for 22 and rank runs in nearly the same order (Spearman 0.93). Only 6% of random 19-task picks track it more closely.

points.title: Cost
points.text: A subset run costs about 15% of a full run; a full run costs a median 6.4× as much. Comparator costs here are the recorded trial costs on the 19 tasks.

points.title: Caveats
points.text: The subset was chosen with this leaderboard in view, so agreement is optimistic for a new model. Subset error bars are wide: about ±10 points.
